newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian PM names two new ministers after scandal.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian PM names two new ministers after scandal.

text.p: Prime Minister Gyula Horn has nominated two ministers to fill posts being vacated by Tamas Suchman, sacked in a scandal over Hungary's privatisation programme, the Hungarian news agency said.

Horn, in an announcement on Wednesday night, said he was appointing Judit Csiha as minister in charge of the state privatisation agency APV Rt and Szabolcs Fazakas to be minister of industry, trade and tourism, the MTI agency said.
Suchman, a close Horn ally who held both posts, was sacked at the weekend following a scandal involving payment of 804 million forints ($5.2 million) in fees to consultant Marta Tocsik.

Tocsik was negotiating lower payments to municipalities for land used by state-owned companies, but a government oversight agency found last week her contract was irregular because it had not been awarded on the basis of competitive bidding.
Horn on Friday sacked the supervisory and executive boards of APV, which had hired Tocsik, and on Sunday sacked Suchman.

Csiha is a political state secretary at the Ministry of Justice and has been involved in the government's negotiations with the Jewish community over the return of Jewish assets confiscated by Hungary's Nazi-aligned government during World War Two.
Fazakas, who is ambassador to Bonn, had been state secretary the Ministry of Industry and Trade.

Horn, who made the announcements in a session of his Hungarian Socialist Party parliamentary group, also said he would nominate Arpad Kovacs for president of the APV board of directors and Andras Laszlo as APV general manager, MTI said.
The nominations are subject to approval by parliament.
